vocabulary.Fitted: inductive : List (Prod Elements.Point (Prod Elements.Point Elements.Point)) → Prop

vocabulary.Figures.crossingCount: def : List Elements.Point → Elements.Point → Elements.Point → Nat := fun (ps : List Elements.Point) (X Q : Elements.Point) => List.length (List.filter (fun (s : Prod Elements.Point Elements.Point) => Decidable.decide (Elements.Figures.RayCrosses X Q s)) (Elements.Figures.sides ps))
vocabulary.Figures.SimpleLoop: def : List Elements.Point → Prop := fun (ps : List Elements.Point) => And (LE.le 3 (List.length ps)) (And (List.Nodup ps) (And (∀ (s : Prod Elements.Point Elements.Point), Membership.mem (Elements.Figures.sides ps) s → Ne (Prod.fst s) (Prod.snd s)) (List.Pairwise (fun (s t : Prod Elements.Point Elements.Point) => ∀ (X : Elements.Point), Elements.OnFiniteLine X (Prod.fst s) (Prod.snd s) → Elements.OnFiniteLine X (Prod.fst t) (Prod.snd t) → And (Or (Eq X (Prod.fst s)) (Eq X (Prod.snd s))) (Or (Eq X (Prod.fst t)) (Eq X (Prod.snd t)))) (Elements.Figures.sides ps))))
vocabulary.Figures.RayCrosses: def : Elements.Point → Elements.Point → Prod Elements.Point Elements.Point → Prop := fun (X Q : Elements.Point) (s : Prod Elements.Point Elements.Point) => Exists fun (Y : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.OnRay Y X Q) (Elements.Between (Prod.fst s) Y (Prod.snd s))
vocabulary.Figures.Outline.mk: constructor : (loops : List (List Elements.Point)) → Ne loops List.nil → (∀ (ps : List Elements.Point), Membership.mem loops ps → Elements.Figures.SimpleLoop ps) → List.Pairwise Elements.Figures.CompatibleLoops loops → Elements.Figures.Outline
vocabulary.Figures.Outline.loops: def : Elements.Figures.Outline → List (List Elements.Point) := fun (self : Elements.Figures.Outline) => self.1
vocabulary.Figures.Outline.depth: def : Elements.Figures.Outline → Elements.Point → Nat := fun (F : Elements.Figures.Outline) (X : Elements.Point) => List.length (List.filter (fun (ps : List Elements.Point) => Decidable.decide (Elements.Figures.LoopInside ps X)) (Elements.Figures.Outline.loops F))
vocabulary.Figures.Outline.area: def : Elements.Figures.Outline → Elements.Area := fun (F : Elements.Figures.Outline) => Classical.epsilon fun (a : Elements.Area) => Exists fun (R : Elements.Apart) => And (Elements.Figures.Divides (Elements.Figures.Outline.Region F) R) (Eq (Elements.Apart.area R) a)
vocabulary.Figures.Outline.Region: def : Elements.Figures.Outline → Elements.Point → Prop := fun (F : Elements.Figures.Outline) (X : Elements.Point) => Or (Elements.Figures.Outline.Boundary F X) (Elements.Figures.Outline.Inside F X)
vocabulary.Figures.Outline.Inside: def : Elements.Figures.Outline → Elements.Point → Prop := fun (F : Elements.Figures.Outline) (X : Elements.Point) => And (Not (Elements.Figures.Outline.Boundary F X)) (Eq (HMod.hMod (Elements.Figures.Outline.depth F X) 2) 1)
vocabulary.Figures.Outline.Boundary: def : Elements.Figures.Outline → Elements.Point → Prop := fun (F : Elements.Figures.Outline) (X : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (ps : List Elements.Point) => And (Membership.mem (Elements.Figures.Outline.loops F) ps) (Elements.Figures.LoopBoundary ps X)
vocabulary.Figures.LoopRegion: def : List Elements.Point → Elements.Point → Prop := fun (ps : List Elements.Point) (X : Elements.Point) => Or (Elements.Figures.LoopBoundary ps X) (Elements.Figures.LoopInside ps X)
vocabulary.Figures.LoopInside: def : List Elements.Point → Elements.Point → Prop := fun (ps : List Elements.Point) (X : Elements.Point) => And (Not (Elements.Figures.LoopBoundary ps X)) (Exists fun (Q : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Figures.GoodRay ps X Q) (Eq (HMod.hMod (Elements.Figures.crossingCount ps X Q) 2) 1))
vocabulary.Figures.LoopBoundary: def : List Elements.Point → Elements.Point → Prop := fun (ps : List Elements.Point) (X : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (s : Prod Elements.Point Elements.Point) => And (Membership.mem (Elements.Figures.sides ps) s) (Elements.OnFiniteLine X (Prod.fst s) (Prod.snd s))
vocabulary.Figures.GoodRay: def : List Elements.Point → Elements.Point → Elements.Point → Prop := fun (ps : List Elements.Point) (X Q : Elements.Point) => And (Ne X Q) (∀ (V : Elements.Point), Membership.mem ps V → Not (Elements.Collinear X Q V))
vocabulary.Figures.Divides: def : (Elements.Point → Prop) → Elements.Apart → Prop := fun (U : Elements.Point → Prop) (R : Elements.Apart) => ∀ (X : Elements.Point), Iff (Elements.Figures.Covers (Elements.Apart.pieces R) X) (U X)
vocabulary.Figures.Covers: def : List (Prod Elements.Point (Prod Elements.Point Elements.Point)) → Elements.Point → Prop := fun (ts : List (Prod Elements.Point (Prod Elements.Point Elements.Point))) (X : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (t : Prod Elements.Point (Prod Elements.Point Elements.Point)) => And (Membership.mem ts t) (Elements.OnOrInsideTriangle X (Prod.fst t) (Prod.fst (Prod.snd t)) (Prod.snd (Prod.snd t)))
vocabulary.Figures.CompatibleLoops: def : List Elements.Point → List Elements.Point → Prop := fun (ps qs : List Elements.Point) => And (∀ (X : Elements.Point), Elements.Figures.LoopBoundary ps X → Elements.Figures.LoopBoundary qs X → Or (Membership.mem ps X) (Membership.mem qs X)) (Or (∀ (X : Elements.Point), Elements.Figures.LoopInside ps X → Not (Elements.Figures.LoopInside qs X)) (Or (∀ (X : Elements.Point), Elements.Figures.LoopRegion ps X → Elements.Figures.LoopRegion qs X) (∀ (X : Elements.Point), Elements.Figures.LoopRegion qs X → Elements.Figures.LoopRegion ps X)))
vocabulary.Equilateral: def : Elements.Point → Elements.Point → Elements.Point → Prop := fun (A B C : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Triangle A B C) (And (Eq (Elements.len A B) (Elements.len B C)) (Eq (Elements.len B C) (Elements.len C A)))
vocabulary.EqualCircles: def : Elements.Circle → Elements.Circle → Prop := fun (α β : Elements.Circle) => Exists fun (G : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (H : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (P : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (Q : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Centre G α) (And (Elements.Centre H β) (And (Elements.OnCircle P α) (And (Elements.OnCircle Q β) (Eq (Elements.len G P) (Elements.len H Q)))))
vocabulary.Corners: def : Prod Elements.Point (Prod Elements.Point Elements.Point) → Elements.Point → Elements.Point → Elements.Point → Prop := fun (t : Prod Elements.Point (Prod Elements.Point Elements.Point)) (P Q R : Elements.Point) => Or (Eq t (Prod.mk P (Prod.mk Q R))) (Or (Eq t (Prod.mk Q (Prod.mk R P))) (Or (Eq t (Prod.mk R (Prod.mk P Q))) (Or (Eq t (Prod.mk Q (Prod.mk P R))) (Or (Eq t (Prod.mk P (Prod.mk R Q))) (Eq t (Prod.mk R (Prod.mk Q P)))))))
vocabulary.Contain: def : Elements.Length → Elements.Length → Elements.Area → Prop := fun (a b : Elements.Length) (x : Elements.Area) => Or (And (Or (Eq a 0) (Eq b 0)) (Eq x 0)) (Exists fun (P : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (Q : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (R : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (S : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Rectangle P Q R S) (And (Eq (Elements.len P Q) a) (And (Eq (Elements.len P S) b) (Eq (Elements.quadArea P Q R S) x))))
vocabulary.Collinear: def : Elements.Point → Elements.Point → Elements.Point → Prop := fun (A B C : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (L : Elements.Line) => And (Elements.OnLine A L) (And (Elements.OnLine B L) (Elements.OnLine C L))
vocabulary.CirclesTouchAt: def : Elements.Circle → Elements.Circle → Elements.Point → Prop := fun (α β : Elements.Circle) (C : Elements.Point) => Or (Elements.TouchesInternallyAt α β C) (Or (Elements.TouchesInternallyAt β α C) (Elements.TouchesExternallyAt α β C))
vocabulary.CirclesTouch: def : Elements.Circle → Elements.Circle → Elements.Point → Prop := fun (α β : Elements.Circle) (C : Elements.Point) => Or (Elements.TouchesInternally α β C) (Or (Elements.TouchesInternally β α C) (Elements.TouchesExternally α β C))
vocabulary.CirclesMeet: def : Elements.Circle → Elements.Circle → Prop := fun (α β : Elements.Circle) => Exists fun (A : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (B : Elements.Point) => And (Ne A B) (And (Elements.OnCircle A α) (And (Elements.OnCircle A β) (And (Elements.OnCircle B α) (Elements.OnCircle B β))))
vocabulary.CirclesCut: def : Elements.Circle → Elements.Circle → Prop := fun (α β : Elements.Circle) => And (Elements.CirclesMeet α β) (And (Exists fun (P : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.OnCircle P α) (Elements.InsideCircle P β)) (Exists fun (P : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.OnCircle P β) (Elements.InsideCircle P α)))
vocabulary.AreParallel: def : Elements.Point → Elements.Point → Elements.Point → Elements.Point → Prop := fun (A B C D : Elements.Point) => And (Ne A B) (And (Ne C D) (∀ (L M : Elements.Line), Elements.OnLine A L → Elements.OnLine B L → Elements.OnLine C M → Elements.OnLine D M → Elements.Parallel L M))

vocabulary.Arc.circle: def : Elements.Arc → Elements.Circle := fun (self : Elements.Arc) => self.1
vocabulary.Arc.Semicircle: def : Elements.Arc → Prop := fun (a : Elements.Arc) => Exists fun (O : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Centre O (Elements.Arc.circle a)) (Elements.Collinear (Elements.Arc.B a) (Elements.Arc.C a) O)
vocabulary.Arc.Less: def : Elements.Arc → Prop := fun (a : Elements.Arc) => Exists fun (O : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Centre O (Elements.Arc.circle a)) (Elements.OppositeSidesOf O (Elements.Arc.K a) (Elements.Arc.B a) (Elements.Arc.C a))
vocabulary.Arc.K: def : Elements.Arc → Elements.Point := fun (self : Elements.Arc) => self.4
vocabulary.Arc.Greater: def : Elements.Arc → Prop := fun (a : Elements.Arc) => Exists fun (O : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Centre O (Elements.Arc.circle a)) (Elements.SameSideOf O (Elements.Arc.K a) (Elements.Arc.B a) (Elements.Arc.C a))
vocabulary.Arc.Drawn: def : Elements.Arc → Prop := fun (a : Elements.Arc) => And (Elements.OnCircle (Elements.Arc.B a) (Elements.Arc.circle a)) (And (Elements.OnCircle (Elements.Arc.C a) (Elements.Arc.circle a)) (Not (Elements.Collinear (Elements.Arc.B a) (Elements.Arc.C a) (Elements.Arc.K a))))
vocabulary.Arc.Congruent: def : Elements.Arc → Elements.Arc → Prop := fun (a b : Elements.Arc) => Exists fun (f : Elements.Point → Elements.Point) => And (Eq (f (Elements.Arc.B a)) (Elements.Arc.B b)) (And (Eq (f (Elements.Arc.C a)) (Elements.Arc.C b)) (And (Elements.Places f (fun (x : Elements.Point) => Elements.InSegment x a) fun (x : Elements.Point) => Elements.InSegment x b) (Elements.Places f (fun (x : Elements.Point) => Elements.OnArc x a) fun (x : Elements.Point) => Elements.OnArc x b)))
vocabulary.Arc.C: def : Elements.Arc → Elements.Point := fun (self : Elements.Arc) => self.3
vocabulary.Arc.B: def : Elements.Arc → Elements.Point := fun (self : Elements.Arc) => self.2

vocabulary.Apart.mk: constructor : (pieces : List (Prod Elements.Point (Prod Elements.Point Elements.Point))) → Ne pieces List.nil → (∀ (t : Prod Elements.Point (Prod Elements.Point Elements.Point)), Membership.mem pieces t → Elements.Triangle (Prod.fst t) (Prod.fst (Prod.snd t)) (Prod.snd (Prod.snd t))) → List.Pairwise (fun (s s' : Prod Elements.Point (Prod Elements.Point Elements.Point)) => ∀ (Y : Elements.Point), Elements.InsideTriangle Y (Prod.fst s) (Prod.fst (Prod.snd s)) (Prod.snd (Prod.snd s)) → Not (Elements.InsideTriangle Y (Prod.fst s') (Prod.fst (Prod.snd s')) (Prod.snd (Prod.snd s')))) pieces → Elements.Apart
vocabulary.Apart.area: def : Elements.Apart → Elements.Area := fun (R : Elements.Apart) => Elements.Magnitude.sum (List.map (fun (t : Prod Elements.Point (Prod Elements.Point Elements.Point)) => Elements.area (Prod.fst t) (Prod.fst (Prod.snd t)) (Prod.snd (Prod.snd t))) (Elements.Apart.pieces R))

propositions.statement: ∀ (A B : Elements.Point), Ne A B → ∀ (P : Elements.Point), Exists fun (C : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Equilateral A B C) (Not (Elements.Collinear A B P) → Elements.SameSideOf C P A B)
propositions.name: BookI.Prop1
propositions.enunciation: On a given finite straight line to construct an equilateral triangle.

propositions.statement: ∀ (A B C : Elements.Point), Ne B C → Exists fun (L : Elements.Point) => Eq (Elements.len A L) (Elements.len B C)
propositions.name: BookI.Prop2
propositions.enunciation:
To place at a given point (as an extremity) a straight line equal to a given straight
line.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C₁ C₂ : Elements.Point}, Ne C₁ C₂ → LT.lt (Elements.len C₁ C₂) (Elements.len A B) → Exists fun (E : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Between A E B) (Eq (Elements.len A E) (Elements.len C₁ C₂))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop3
propositions.enunciation:
Given two unequal straight lines, to cut off from the greater a straight line equal to the
less.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Elements.Triangle D E F → Eq (Elements.len A B) (Elements.len D E) → Eq (Elements.len A C) (Elements.len D F) → Eq (Elements.ang B A C) (Elements.ang E D F) → And (Eq (Elements.len B C) (Elements.len E F)) (And (Eq (Elements.area A B C) (Elements.area D E F)) (And (Eq (Elements.ang A B C) (Elements.ang D E F)) (Eq (Elements.ang A C B) (Elements.ang D F E))))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop4
propositions.enunciation:
If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles
contained by the equal straight lines equal, they will also have the base equal to the base, the
triangle will be equal to the triangle, and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining
angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Eq (Elements.len A B) (Elements.len A C) → Elements.Between A B D → Elements.Between A C E → And (Eq (Elements.ang A B C) (Elements.ang A C B)) (Eq (Elements.ang C B D) (Elements.ang B C E))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop5
propositions.enunciation:
In isosceles triangles the angles at the base are equal to one another, and, if the equal
straight lines be produced further, the angles under the base will be equal to one another.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Eq (Elements.ang A B C) (Elements.ang A C B) → Eq (Elements.len A B) (Elements.len A C)
propositions.name: BookI.Prop6
propositions.enunciation:
If in a triangle two angles be equal to one another, the sides which subtend the equal angles
will also be equal to one another.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point}, Elements.SameSideOf C D A B → Eq (Elements.len C A) (Elements.len D A) → Eq (Elements.len C B) (Elements.len D B) → Eq C D
propositions.name: BookI.Prop7
propositions.enunciation:
Given two straight lines constructed on a straight line (from its extremities) and meeting in a
point, there cannot be constructed on the same straight line (from its extremities), and on the
same side of it, two other straight lines meeting in another point and equal to the former two
respectively, namely each to that which has the same extremity with it.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Elements.Triangle D E F → Eq (Elements.len A B) (Elements.len D E) → Eq (Elements.len A C) (Elements.len D F) → Eq (Elements.len B C) (Elements.len E F) → Eq (Elements.ang B A C) (Elements.ang E D F)
propositions.name: BookI.Prop8
propositions.enunciation:
If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have also the base
equal to the base, they will also have the angles equal which are contained by the equal
straight lines.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle B A C → Exists fun (F : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.SameSideOf F C A B) (And (Elements.SameSideOf F B A C) (And (Eq (Elements.ang B A F) (Elements.ang F A C)) (Eq (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.ang B A F) (Elements.ang F A C)) (Elements.ang B A C))))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop9
propositions.enunciation: To bisect a given rectilineal angle.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B : Elements.Point}, Ne A B → Exists fun (D : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Between A D B) (Eq (Elements.len A D) (Elements.len D B))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop10
propositions.enunciation: To bisect a given finite straight line.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C Q : Elements.Point}, Ne A B → Elements.Collinear A B C → Not (Elements.Collinear A B Q) → Exists fun (F : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.SameSideOf F Q A B) (∀ (P : Elements.Point), Elements.Collinear A B P → Ne P C → Eq (Elements.ang P C F) Elements.rightAngle)
propositions.name: BookI.Prop11
propositions.enunciation: To draw a straight line at right angles to a given straight line from a given point on it.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C : Elements.Point}, Ne A B → Not (Elements.Collinear A B C) → Exists fun (H : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Collinear A B H) (∀ (P : Elements.Point), Elements.Collinear A B P → Ne P H → Eq (Elements.ang C H P) Elements.rightAngle)
propositions.name: BookI.Prop12
propositions.enunciation:
To a given infinite straight line, from a given point which is not on it, to draw a
perpendicular straight line.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point}, Elements.Between C B D → Not (Elements.Collinear C D A) → Eq (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.ang C B A) (Elements.ang A B D)) (HAdd.hAdd Elements.rightAngle Elements.rightAngle)
propositions.name: BookI.Prop13
propositions.enunciation:
If a straight line set up on a straight line make angles, it will make either two right angles
or angles equal to two right angles.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point}, Elements.OppositeSidesOf C D A B → Eq (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.ang A B C) (Elements.ang A B D)) (HAdd.hAdd Elements.rightAngle Elements.rightAngle) → Elements.Between C B D
propositions.name: BookI.Prop14
propositions.enunciation:
If with any straight line, and at a point on it, two straight lines not lying on the same side
make the adjacent angles equal to two right angles, the two straight lines will be in a straight
line with one another.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E : Elements.Point}, Elements.Between A E B → Elements.Between C E D → Not (Elements.Collinear A B C) → And (Eq (Elements.ang A E C) (Elements.ang D E B)) (Eq (Elements.ang C E B) (Elements.ang A E D))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop15
propositions.enunciation: If two straight lines cut one another, they make the vertical angles equal to one another.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Elements.Between B C D → And (LT.lt (Elements.ang C B A) (Elements.ang A C D)) (LT.lt (Elements.ang B A C) (Elements.ang A C D))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop16
propositions.enunciation:
In any triangle, if one of the sides be produced, the exterior angle is greater than either of
the interior and opposite angles.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → And (LT.lt (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.ang A B C) (Elements.ang B C A)) (HAdd.hAdd Elements.rightAngle Elements.rightAngle)) (And (LT.lt (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.ang B A C) (Elements.ang A C B)) (HAdd.hAdd Elements.rightAngle Elements.rightAngle)) (LT.lt (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.ang C A B) (Elements.ang A B C)) (HAdd.hAdd Elements.rightAngle Elements.rightAngle)))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop17
propositions.enunciation: In any triangle two angles taken together in any manner are less than two right angles.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → LT.lt (Elements.len A B) (Elements.len A C) → LT.lt (Elements.ang B C A) (Elements.ang A B C)
propositions.name: BookI.Prop18
propositions.enunciation: In any triangle the greater side subtends the greater angle.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → LT.lt (Elements.ang B C A) (Elements.ang A B C) → LT.lt (Elements.len A B) (Elements.len A C)
propositions.name: BookI.Prop19
propositions.enunciation: In any triangle the greater angle is subtended by the greater side.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → And (LT.lt (Elements.len B C) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.len B A) (Elements.len A C))) (And (LT.lt (Elements.len A C) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.len A B) (Elements.len B C))) (LT.lt (Elements.len A B) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.len B C) (Elements.len C A))))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop20
propositions.enunciation: In any triangle two sides taken together in any manner are greater than the remaining one.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Elements.InsideTriangle D A B C → And (LT.lt (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.len B D) (Elements.len D C)) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.len B A) (Elements.len A C))) (LT.lt (Elements.ang B A C) (Elements.ang B D C))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop21
propositions.enunciation:
If on one of the sides of a triangle, from its extremities, there be constructed two straight
lines meeting within the triangle, the straight lines so constructed will be less than the
remaining two sides of the triangle, but will contain a greater angle.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A₁ A₂ B₁ B₂ C₁ C₂ E F P : Elements.Point}, LT.lt (Elements.len C₁ C₂) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.len A₁ A₂) (Elements.len B₁ B₂)) → LT.lt (Elements.len B₁ B₂) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.len A₁ A₂) (Elements.len C₁ C₂)) → LT.lt (Elements.len A₁ A₂) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.len B₁ B₂) (Elements.len C₁ C₂)) → Ne F E → Not (Elements.Collinear F E P) → Exists fun (G : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (K : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.OnRay G F E) (And (Elements.SameSideOf K P F E) (And (Eq (Elements.len K F) (Elements.len A₁ A₂)) (And (Eq (Elements.len F G) (Elements.len B₁ B₂)) (Eq (Elements.len G K) (Elements.len C₁ C₂)))))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop22
propositions.enunciation:
Out of three straight lines, which are equal to three given straight lines, to construct a
triangle: thus it is necessary that two of the straight lines taken together in any manner
should be greater than the remaining one. [I. 20]

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E P : Elements.Point}, Ne A B → Elements.Triangle D C E → Not (Elements.Collinear A B P) → Exists fun (F : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (G : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.OnRay G A B) (And (Elements.SameSideOf F P A B) (Eq (Elements.ang F A G) (Elements.ang D C E)))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop23
propositions.enunciation:
On a given straight line and at a point on it to construct a rectilineal angle equal to a given
rectilineal angle.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Elements.Triangle D E F → Eq (Elements.len A B) (Elements.len D E) → Eq (Elements.len A C) (Elements.len D F) → LT.lt (Elements.ang E D F) (Elements.ang B A C) → LT.lt (Elements.len E F) (Elements.len B C)
propositions.name: BookI.Prop24
propositions.enunciation:
If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, but have the one of the
angles contained by the equal straight lines greater than the other, they will also have the
base greater than the base.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Elements.Triangle D E F → Eq (Elements.len A B) (Elements.len D E) → Eq (Elements.len A C) (Elements.len D F) → LT.lt (Elements.len E F) (Elements.len B C) → LT.lt (Elements.ang E D F) (Elements.ang B A C)
propositions.name: BookI.Prop25
propositions.enunciation:
If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, but have the base greater
than the base, they will also have the one of the angles contained by the equal straight lines
greater than the other.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Elements.Triangle D E F → Eq (Elements.ang A B C) (Elements.ang D E F) → Eq (Elements.ang B C A) (Elements.ang E F D) → Or (Eq (Elements.len B C) (Elements.len E F)) (Eq (Elements.len A B) (Elements.len D E)) → And (Eq (Elements.len A B) (Elements.len D E)) (And (Eq (Elements.len A C) (Elements.len D F)) (And (Eq (Elements.len B C) (Elements.len E F)) (Eq (Elements.ang B A C) (Elements.ang E D F))))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop26
propositions.enunciation:
If two triangles have the two angles equal to two angles respectively, and one side equal to one
side, namely, either the side adjoining the equal angles, or that subtending one of the equal
angles, they will also have the remaining sides equal to the remaining sides and the remaining
angle to the remaining angle.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F : Elements.Point}, Elements.Between A E B → Elements.Between C F D → Elements.OppositeSidesOf A D E F → Eq (Elements.ang A E F) (Elements.ang E F D) → Elements.AreParallel A B C D
propositions.name: BookI.Prop27
propositions.enunciation:
If a straight line falling on two straight lines make the alternate angles equal to one another,
the straight lines will be parallel to one another.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F G H : Elements.Point}, Elements.Between A G B → Elements.Between C H D → Elements.Between E G H → Elements.Between G H F → Elements.SameSideOf B D E F → Or (Eq (Elements.ang E G B) (Elements.ang G H D)) (Eq (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.ang B G H) (Elements.ang G H D)) (HAdd.hAdd Elements.rightAngle Elements.rightAngle)) → Elements.AreParallel A B C D
propositions.name: BookI.Prop28
propositions.enunciation:
If a straight line falling on two straight lines make the exterior angle equal to the interior
and opposite angle on the same side, or the interior angles on the same side equal to two right
angles, the straight lines will be parallel to one another.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F G H : Elements.Point}, Elements.AreParallel A B C D → Elements.Between A G B → Elements.Between C H D → Elements.Between E G H → Elements.Between G H F → Elements.SameSideOf B D E F → And (Eq (Elements.ang A G H) (Elements.ang G H D)) (And (Eq (Elements.ang E G B) (Elements.ang G H D)) (Eq (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.ang B G H) (Elements.ang G H D)) (HAdd.hAdd Elements.rightAngle Elements.rightAngle)))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop29
propositions.enunciation:
A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one
another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on
the same side equal to two right angles.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F : Elements.Point}, Elements.AreParallel A B E F → Elements.AreParallel C D E F → Not (Elements.Collinear A B C) → Elements.AreParallel A B C D
propositions.name: BookI.Prop30
propositions.enunciation: Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C : Elements.Point}, Ne B C → Not (Elements.Collinear B C A) → Exists fun (E : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (F : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Between E A F) (Elements.AreParallel E F B C)
propositions.name: BookI.Prop31
propositions.enunciation: Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Elements.Between B C D → And (Eq (Elements.ang A C D) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.ang C A B) (Elements.ang A B C))) (Eq (HAdd.hAdd (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.ang A B C) (Elements.ang B C A)) (Elements.ang C A B)) (HAdd.hAdd Elements.rightAngle Elements.rightAngle))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop32
propositions.enunciation:
In any triangle, if one of the sides be produced, the exterior angle is equal to the two
interior and opposite angles, and the three interior angles of the triangle are equal to two
right angles.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point}, Elements.AreParallel A B C D → Eq (Elements.len A B) (Elements.len C D) → Elements.SameSideOf B D A C → And (Eq (Elements.len A C) (Elements.len B D)) (Elements.AreParallel A C B D)
propositions.name: BookI.Prop33
propositions.enunciation:
The straight lines joining equal and parallel straight lines (at the extremities which are) in
the same directions (respectively) are themselves also equal and parallel.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point}, Elements.Parallelogram A C D B → And (Eq (Elements.len A B) (Elements.len C D)) (And (Eq (Elements.len A C) (Elements.len B D)) (And (Eq (Elements.ang B A C) (Elements.ang C D B)) (And (Eq (Elements.ang A B D) (Elements.ang A C D)) (Eq (Elements.area A B C) (Elements.area D C B)))))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop34
propositions.enunciation:
In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the
diameter bisects the areas.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F : Elements.Point}, Elements.Parallelogram A B C D → Elements.Parallelogram E B C F → (Exists fun (L : Elements.Line) => And (Elements.OnLine A L) (And (Elements.OnLine D L) (And (Elements.OnLine E L) (Elements.OnLine F L)))) → Eq (Elements.quadArea A B C D) (Elements.quadArea E B C F)
propositions.name: BookI.Prop35
propositions.enunciation: Parallelograms which are on the same base and in the same parallels are equal to one another.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F G H : Elements.Point}, Elements.Parallelogram A B C D → Elements.Parallelogram E F G H → Eq (Elements.len B C) (Elements.len F G) → (Exists fun (L : Elements.Line) => And (Elements.OnLine A L) (And (Elements.OnLine D L) (And (Elements.OnLine E L) (Elements.OnLine H L)))) → (Exists fun (L : Elements.Line) => And (Elements.OnLine B L) (And (Elements.OnLine C L) (And (Elements.OnLine F L) (Elements.OnLine G L)))) → Eq (Elements.quadArea A B C D) (Elements.quadArea E F G H)
propositions.name: BookI.Prop36
propositions.enunciation: Parallelograms which are on equal bases and in the same parallels are equal to one another.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Elements.Triangle D B C → (Exists fun (L : Elements.Line) => Exists fun (M : Elements.Line) => And (Elements.Parallel L M) (And (Elements.OnLine A L) (And (Elements.OnLine D L) (And (Elements.OnLine B M) (Elements.OnLine C M))))) → Eq (Elements.area A B C) (Elements.area D B C)
propositions.name: BookI.Prop37
propositions.enunciation: Triangles which are on the same base and in the same parallels are equal to one another.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Elements.Triangle D E F → Eq (Elements.len B C) (Elements.len E F) → (Exists fun (L : Elements.Line) => Exists fun (M : Elements.Line) => And (Elements.Parallel L M) (And (Elements.OnLine A L) (And (Elements.OnLine D L) (And (Elements.OnLine B M) (And (Elements.OnLine C M) (And (Elements.OnLine E M) (Elements.OnLine F M))))))) → Eq (Elements.area A B C) (Elements.area D E F)
propositions.name: BookI.Prop38
propositions.enunciation: Triangles which are on equal bases and in the same parallels are equal to one another.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Elements.Triangle D B C → Eq (Elements.area A B C) (Elements.area D B C) → Elements.SameSideOf A D B C → Ne A D → Elements.AreParallel A D B C
propositions.name: BookI.Prop39
propositions.enunciation: Equal triangles which are on the same base and on the same side are also in the same parallels.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Elements.Triangle C D E → Elements.Between B C E → Eq (Elements.len B C) (Elements.len C E) → Eq (Elements.area A B C) (Elements.area C D E) → Elements.SameSideOf A D B E → Ne A D → Elements.AreParallel A D B E
propositions.name: BookI.Prop40
propositions.enunciation: Equal triangles which are on equal bases and on the same side are also in the same parallels.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E : Elements.Point}, Elements.Parallelogram A B C D → Elements.Collinear A D E → Eq (Elements.quadArea A B C D) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.area B E C) (Elements.area B E C))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop41
propositions.enunciation:
If a parallelogram have the same base with a triangle and be in the same parallels, the
parallelogram is double of the triangle.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D₁ D D₂ : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Elements.Triangle D₁ D D₂ → Exists fun (E : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (F : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (G : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Between B E C) (And (Elements.SameSideOf F A B C) (And (Elements.Parallelogram F E C G) (And (Eq (Elements.ang C E F) (Elements.ang D₁ D D₂)) (Eq (Elements.quadArea F E C G) (Elements.area A B C)))))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop42
propositions.enunciation: To construct, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given triangle.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F G H K : Elements.Point}, Elements.Parallelogram A B C D → Elements.Between A K C → Elements.Between A E B → Elements.Between B G C → Elements.Between C F D → Elements.Between D H A → Elements.Parallelogram A E K H → Elements.Parallelogram K G C F → Eq (Elements.quadArea E B G K) (Elements.quadArea H K F D)
propositions.name: BookI.Prop43
propositions.enunciation:
In any parallelogram the complements of the parallelograms about the diameter are equal to one
another.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C₁ C₂ C₃ D₁ D D₂ P : Elements.Point}, Ne A B → Elements.Triangle C₁ C₂ C₃ → Elements.Triangle D₁ D D₂ → Not (Elements.Collinear A B P) → Exists fun (L : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (M : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.SameSideOf M P A B) (And (Elements.Parallelogram A B M L) (And (Eq (Elements.ang A B M) (Elements.ang D₁ D D₂)) (Eq (Elements.quadArea A B M L) (Elements.area C₁ C₂ C₃))))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop44
propositions.enunciation:
To a given straight line to apply, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a
given triangle.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E₁ E E₂ : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B D → Elements.Triangle D B C → Elements.Triangle E₁ E E₂ → Exists fun (K : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (F : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (L : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (M : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Parallelogram K F L M) (And (Eq (Elements.ang F K M) (Elements.ang E₁ E E₂)) (Eq (Elements.quadArea K F L M) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.area A B D) (Elements.area D B C))))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop45
propositions.enunciation: To construct, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given rectilineal figure.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B P : Elements.Point}, Ne A B → Not (Elements.Collinear A B P) → Exists fun (D : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (E : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Square A D E B) (And (Elements.SameSideOf D P A B) (Elements.SameSideOf E P A B))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop46
propositions.enunciation: On a given straight line to describe a square.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F G H K : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Eq (Elements.ang B A C) Elements.rightAngle → Elements.Square B D E C → Elements.OppositeSidesOf D A B C → Elements.OppositeSidesOf E A B C → Elements.Square A B F G → Elements.OppositeSidesOf F C A B → Elements.OppositeSidesOf G C A B → Elements.Square A C K H → Elements.OppositeSidesOf K B A C → Elements.OppositeSidesOf H B A C → Eq (Elements.quadArea B D E C) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.quadArea A B F G) (Elements.quadArea A C K H))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop47
propositions.enunciation:
In right-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the right angle is equal to the
squares on the sides containing the right angle.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C P Q R S T U : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Elements.Square B P Q C → Elements.SameSideOf P Q B C → Elements.Square A B R S → Elements.SameSideOf R S A B → Elements.Square A C T U → Elements.SameSideOf T U A C → Eq (Elements.quadArea B P Q C) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.quadArea A B R S) (Elements.quadArea A C T U)) → Eq (Elements.ang B A C) Elements.rightAngle
propositions.name: BookI.Prop48
propositions.enunciation:
If in a triangle the square on one of the sides be equal to the squares on the remaining two
sides of the triangle, the angle contained by the remaining two sides of the triangle is right.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A₁ A₂ B C D E : Elements.Point}, Ne A₁ A₂ → Elements.Between B D E → Elements.Between D E C → Eq (Elements.rect A₁ A₂ B C) (HAdd.hAdd (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.rect A₁ A₂ B D) (Elements.rect A₁ A₂ D E)) (Elements.rect A₁ A₂ E C))
propositions.name: BookII.Prop1
propositions.enunciation:
If there be two straight lines, and one of them be cut into any number of segments whatever, the
rectangle contained by the two straight lines is equal to the rectangles contained by the uncut
straight line and each of the segments.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C : Elements.Point}, Elements.Between A C B → Eq (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.rect A B B C) (Elements.rect B A A C)) (Elements.sq A B)
propositions.name: BookII.Prop2
propositions.enunciation:
If a straight line be cut at random, the rectangle contained by the whole and both of the
segments is equal to the square on the whole.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C : Elements.Point}, Elements.Between A C B → Eq (Elements.rect A B B C) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.rect A C C B) (Elements.sq B C))
propositions.name: BookII.Prop3
propositions.enunciation:
If a straight line be cut at random, the rectangle contained by the whole and one of the
segments is equal to the rectangle contained by the segments and the square on the aforesaid
segment.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C : Elements.Point}, Elements.Between A C B → Eq (Elements.sq A B) (HAdd.hAdd (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.sq A C) (Elements.sq C B)) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.rect A C C B) (Elements.rect A C C B)))
propositions.name: BookII.Prop4
propositions.enunciation:
If a straight line be cut at random, the square on the whole is equal to the squares on the
segments and twice the rectangle contained by the segments.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point}, Elements.Between A C B → Eq (Elements.len A C) (Elements.len C B) → Elements.Between A D B → Ne D C → Eq (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.rect A D D B) (Elements.sq C D)) (Elements.sq C B)
propositions.name: BookII.Prop5
propositions.enunciation:
If a straight line be cut into equal and unequal segments, the rectangle contained by the
unequal segments of the whole together with the square on the straight line between the points
of section is equal to the square on the half.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point}, Elements.Between A C B → Eq (Elements.len A C) (Elements.len C B) → Elements.Between A B D → Eq (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.rect A D D B) (Elements.sq C B)) (Elements.sq C D)
propositions.name: BookII.Prop6
propositions.enunciation:
If a straight line be bisected and a straight line be added to it in a straight line, the
rectangle contained by the whole with the added straight line and the added straight line
together with the square on the half is equal to the square on the straight line made up of the
half and the added straight line.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C : Elements.Point}, Elements.Between A C B → Eq (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.sq A B) (Elements.sq B C)) (HAdd.hAdd (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.rect A B B C) (Elements.rect A B B C)) (Elements.sq C A))
propositions.name: BookII.Prop7
propositions.enunciation:
If a straight line be cut at random, the square on the whole and that on one of the segments
both together are equal to twice the rectangle contained by the whole and the said segment and
the square on the remaining segment.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C : Elements.Point}, Elements.Between A C B → ∀ (D : Elements.Point), Elements.Between A B D → Eq (Elements.len B D) (Elements.len C B) → Eq (HAdd.hAdd (HAdd.hAdd (HAdd.hAdd (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.rect A B B C) (Elements.rect A B B C)) (Elements.rect A B B C)) (Elements.rect A B B C)) (Elements.sq A C)) (Elements.sq A D)
propositions.name: BookII.Prop8
propositions.enunciation:
If a straight line be cut at random, four times the rectangle contained by the whole and one of
the segments together with the square on the remaining segment is equal to the square described
on the whole and the aforesaid segment as on one straight line.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point}, Elements.Between A C B → Eq (Elements.len A C) (Elements.len C B) → Elements.Between A D B → Ne D C → Eq (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.sq A D) (Elements.sq D B)) (HAdd.hAdd (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.sq A C) (Elements.sq C D)) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.sq A C) (Elements.sq C D)))
propositions.name: BookII.Prop9
propositions.enunciation:
If a straight line be cut into equal and unequal segments, the squares on the unequal segments
of the whole are double of the square on the half and of the square on the straight line between
the points of section.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point}, Elements.Between A C B → Eq (Elements.len A C) (Elements.len C B) → Elements.Between A B D → Eq (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.sq A D) (Elements.sq D B)) (HAdd.hAdd (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.sq A C) (Elements.sq C D)) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.sq A C) (Elements.sq C D)))
propositions.name: BookII.Prop10
propositions.enunciation:
If a straight line be bisected, and a straight line be added to it in a straight line, the
square on the whole with the added straight line and the square on the added straight line both
together are double of the square on the half and of the square described on the straight line
made up of the half and the added straight line as on one straight line.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B : Elements.Point}, Ne A B → Exists fun (H : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Between A H B) (Eq (Elements.rect A B B H) (Elements.sq A H))
propositions.name: BookII.Prop11
propositions.enunciation:
To cut a given straight line so that the rectangle contained by the whole and one of the
segments is equal to the square on the remaining segment.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Elements.IsObtuse B A C → Elements.Collinear C A D → (∀ (P : Elements.Point), Elements.Collinear C A P → Ne P D → Eq (Elements.ang B D P) Elements.rightAngle) → Eq (Elements.sq B C) (HAdd.hAdd (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.sq B A) (Elements.sq A C)) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.rect C A A D) (Elements.rect C A A D)))
propositions.name: BookII.Prop12
propositions.enunciation:
In obtuse-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the obtuse angle is greater than
the squares on the sides containing the obtuse angle by twice the rectangle contained by one of
the sides about the obtuse angle, namely that on which the perpendicular falls, and the straight
line cut off outside by the perpendicular towards the obtuse angle.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Elements.IsAcute A B C → Elements.IsAcute A C B → Elements.Collinear B C D → (∀ (P : Elements.Point), Elements.Collinear B C P → Ne P D → Eq (Elements.ang A D P) Elements.rightAngle) → Eq (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.sq A C) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.rect C B B D) (Elements.rect C B B D))) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.sq C B) (Elements.sq B A))
propositions.name: BookII.Prop13
propositions.enunciation:
In acute-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the acute angle is less than the
squares on the sides containing the acute angle by twice the rectangle contained by one of the
sides about the acute angle, namely that on which the perpendicular falls, and the straight line
cut off within by the perpendicular towards the acute angle.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A₁ A₂ A₃ A₄ : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A₁ A₂ A₄ → Elements.Triangle A₄ A₂ A₃ → Exists fun (E : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (H : Elements.Point) => Eq (Elements.sq E H) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.area A₁ A₂ A₄) (Elements.area A₄ A₂ A₃))
propositions.name: BookII.Prop14
propositions.enunciation: To construct a square equal to a given rectilineal figure.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B : Elements.Point} {ABC : Elements.Circle}, Elements.OnCircle A ABC → Elements.OnCircle B ABC → Ne A B → Exists fun (F : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (C : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (D : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (E : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Centre F ABC) (And (Elements.Between A D B) (And (Eq (Elements.len A D) (Elements.len D B)) (And (Elements.OnCircle C ABC) (And (Elements.OnCircle E ABC) (And (Elements.Between C D E) (And (Eq (Elements.ang A D C) Elements.rightAngle) (And (Elements.Between C F E) (Eq (Elements.len C F) (Elements.len F E)))))))))
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop1
propositions.enunciation: To find the centre of a given circle.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B : Elements.Point} {ABC : Elements.Circle}, Elements.OnCircle A ABC → Elements.OnCircle B ABC → ∀ (E : Elements.Point), Elements.Between A E B → Elements.InsideCircle E ABC
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop2
propositions.enunciation:
If on the circumference of a circle two points be taken at random, the straight line joining the
points will fall within the circle.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B E F : Elements.Point} {ABC : Elements.Circle}, Elements.Centre E ABC → Elements.OnCircle A ABC → Elements.OnCircle B ABC → Elements.Between A F B → Not (Elements.Collinear A B E) → And (Eq (Elements.len A F) (Elements.len F B) → And (Eq (Elements.ang A F E) Elements.rightAngle) (Eq (Elements.ang B F E) Elements.rightAngle)) (Eq (Elements.ang A F E) Elements.rightAngle → Eq (Elements.len A F) (Elements.len F B))
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop3
propositions.enunciation:
If in a circle a straight line through the centre bisect a straight line not through the centre,
it also cuts it at right angles; and if it cut it at right angles, it also bisects it.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E : Elements.Point} {ABCD : Elements.Circle}, Elements.OnCircle A ABCD → Elements.OnCircle B ABCD → Elements.OnCircle C ABCD → Elements.OnCircle D ABCD → Elements.Between A E C → Elements.Between B E D → Not (Elements.Collinear A C B) → (∀ (F : Elements.Point), Elements.Centre F ABCD → Not (Elements.Collinear A C F)) → (∀ (F : Elements.Point), Elements.Centre F ABCD → Not (Elements.Collinear B D F)) → Not (And (Eq (Elements.len A E) (Elements.len E C)) (Eq (Elements.len B E) (Elements.len E D)))
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop4
propositions.enunciation:
If in a circle two straight lines cut one another which are not through the centre, they do not
bisect one another.

propositions.statement: ∀ {E : Elements.Point} {ABC CDG : Elements.Circle}, Elements.CirclesCut ABC CDG → Not (And (Elements.Centre E ABC) (Elements.Centre E CDG))
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop5
propositions.enunciation: If two circles cut one another, they will not have the same centre.

propositions.statement: ∀ {C F : Elements.Point} {ABC CDE : Elements.Circle}, Elements.CirclesTouch ABC CDE C → Not (And (Elements.Centre F ABC) (Elements.Centre F CDE))
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop6
propositions.enunciation: If two circles touch one another, they will not have the same centre.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A D E F : Elements.Point} {ABCD : Elements.Circle}, Elements.Centre E ABCD → Elements.OnCircle A ABCD → Elements.OnCircle D ABCD → Elements.Between A E D → Elements.Between E F D → And (∀ (B : Elements.Point), Elements.OnCircle B ABCD → Ne B A → LT.lt (Elements.len F B) (Elements.len F A)) (And (∀ (G : Elements.Point), Elements.OnCircle G ABCD → Ne G D → LT.lt (Elements.len F D) (Elements.len F G)) (And (∀ (B C : Elements.Point), Elements.OnCircle B ABCD → Elements.OnCircle C ABCD → Elements.SameSideOf B C A D → LT.lt (Elements.ang A F B) (Elements.ang A F C) → LT.lt (Elements.len F C) (Elements.len F B)) (∀ (G : Elements.Point), Elements.OnCircle G ABCD → Not (Elements.Collinear A D G) → Exists fun (H : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.OnCircle H ABCD) (And (Elements.OppositeSidesOf H G A D) (And (Eq (Elements.len F H) (Elements.len F G)) (∀ (K : Elements.Point), Elements.OnCircle K ABCD → Eq (Elements.len F K) (Elements.len F G) → Or (Eq K G) (Eq K H)))))))
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop7
propositions.enunciation:
If on the diameter of a circle a point be taken which is not the centre of the circle, and from
the point straight lines fall upon the circle, that will be greatest on which the centre is, the
remainder of the same diameter will be least, and of the rest the nearer to the straight line
through the centre is always greater than the more remote, and only two equal straight lines
will fall from the point on the circle, one on each side of the least straight line.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A D G : Elements.Point} {ABC : Elements.Circle}, Elements.OutsideCircle D ABC → Elements.OnCircle A ABC → Elements.OnCircle G ABC → Elements.Between D G A → (∀ (M : Elements.Point), Elements.Centre M ABC → Elements.Between G M A) → And (∀ (E : Elements.Point), Elements.OnCircle E ABC → Ne E A → LT.lt (Elements.len D E) (Elements.len D A)) (And (∀ (E F : Elements.Point), Elements.OnCircle E ABC → Elements.OnCircle F ABC → (Exists fun (H : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.OnCircle H ABC) (Elements.Between D H E)) → (Exists fun (L : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.OnCircle L ABC) (Elements.Between D L F)) → Elements.SameSideOf E F D A → LT.lt (Elements.ang A D E) (Elements.ang A D F) → LT.lt (Elements.len D F) (Elements.len D E)) (And (∀ (K : Elements.Point), Elements.OnCircle K ABC → Ne K G → LT.lt (Elements.len D G) (Elements.len D K)) (And (∀ (K L : Elements.Point), Elements.OnCircle K ABC → Elements.OnCircle L ABC → (Exists fun (C : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.OnCircle C ABC) (Elements.Between D K C)) → (Exists fun (F : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.OnCircle F ABC) (Elements.Between D L F)) → Elements.SameSideOf K L D A → LT.lt (Elements.ang A D K) (Elements.ang A D L) → LT.lt (Elements.len D K) (Elements.len D L)) (∀ (K : Elements.Point), Elements.OnCircle K ABC → Not (Elements.Collinear D A K) → Exists fun (B : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.OnCircle B ABC) (And (Elements.OppositeSidesOf B K D A) (And (Eq (Elements.len D B) (Elements.len D K)) (∀ (N : Elements.Point), Elements.OnCircle N ABC → Eq (Elements.len D N) (Elements.len D K) → Or (Eq N K) (Eq N B))))))))
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop8
propositions.enunciation:
If a point be taken outside a circle and from the point straight lines be drawn through to the
circle, one of which is through the centre and the others are drawn at random, then, of the
straight lines which fall on the concave circumference, that through the centre is greatest,
while of the rest the nearer to that through the centre is always greater than the more remote,
but, of the straight lines falling on the convex circumference, that between the point and the
diameter is least, while of the rest the nearer to the least is always less than the more
remote, and only two equal straight lines will fall on the circle from the point, one on each
side of the least.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point} {ABC : Elements.Circle}, Elements.OnCircle A ABC → Elements.OnCircle B ABC → Elements.OnCircle C ABC → Ne A B → Ne B C → Ne A C → Eq (Elements.len D A) (Elements.len D B) → Eq (Elements.len D B) (Elements.len D C) → Elements.Centre D ABC
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop9
propositions.enunciation:
If a point be taken within a circle, and more than two equal straight lines fall from the point
on the circle, the point taken is the centre of the circle.

propositions.statement: ∀ {B G H : Elements.Point} {ABC DEF : Elements.Circle}, Elements.OnCircle B ABC → Elements.OnCircle B DEF → Elements.OnCircle G ABC → Elements.OnCircle G DEF → Elements.OnCircle H ABC → Elements.OnCircle H DEF → Ne B G → Ne B H → Ne G H → Eq ABC DEF
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop10
propositions.enunciation: A circle does not cut a circle at more points than two.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A F G : Elements.Point} {ABC ADE : Elements.Circle}, Elements.Centre F ABC → Elements.Centre G ADE → Elements.TouchesInternally ABC ADE A → Elements.Between F G A
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop11
propositions.enunciation:
If two circles touch one another internally, and their centres be taken, the straight line
joining their centres, if it be also produced, will fall on the point of contact of the circles.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A F G : Elements.Point} {ABC ADE : Elements.Circle}, Elements.Centre F ABC → Elements.Centre G ADE → Elements.TouchesExternally ABC ADE A → Elements.Between F A G
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop12
propositions.enunciation:
If two circles touch one another externally, the straight line joining their centres will pass
through the point of contact.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point} {ABDC EBFD ACK : Elements.Circle}, And (Or (Elements.TouchesInternally ABDC EBFD D) (Elements.TouchesInternally EBFD ABDC D) → Elements.OnCircle B ABDC → Elements.OnCircle B EBFD → Eq B D) (Elements.TouchesExternally ACK ABDC A → Elements.OnCircle C ACK → Elements.OnCircle C ABDC → Eq C A)
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop13
propositions.enunciation:
A circle does not touch a circle at more points than one, whether it touch it internally or
externally.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F G : Elements.Point} {ABDC : Elements.Circle}, Elements.Centre E ABDC → Elements.OnCircle A ABDC → Elements.OnCircle B ABDC → Elements.OnCircle C ABDC → Elements.OnCircle D ABDC → Not (Elements.Collinear A B E) → Not (Elements.Collinear C D E) → Elements.Collinear A B F → (∀ (P : Elements.Point), Elements.Collinear A B P → Ne P F → Eq (Elements.ang E F P) Elements.rightAngle) → Elements.Collinear C D G → (∀ (P : Elements.Point), Elements.Collinear C D P → Ne P G → Eq (Elements.ang E G P) Elements.rightAngle) → Iff (Eq (Elements.len A B) (Elements.len C D)) (Eq (Elements.len E F) (Elements.len E G))
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop14
propositions.enunciation:
In a circle equal straight lines are equally distant from the centre, and those which are
equally distant from the centre are equal to one another.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F G H K : Elements.Point} {ABCD : Elements.Circle}, Elements.Centre E ABCD → Elements.OnCircle A ABCD → Elements.OnCircle D ABCD → Elements.Between A E D → Elements.OnCircle B ABCD → Elements.OnCircle C ABCD → Elements.OnCircle F ABCD → Elements.OnCircle G ABCD → Not (Elements.Collinear B C E) → Not (Elements.Collinear F G E) → Elements.Collinear B C H → (∀ (P : Elements.Point), Elements.Collinear B C P → Ne P H → Eq (Elements.ang E H P) Elements.rightAngle) → Elements.Collinear F G K → (∀ (P : Elements.Point), Elements.Collinear F G P → Ne P K → Eq (Elements.ang E K P) Elements.rightAngle) → LT.lt (Elements.len E H) (Elements.len E K) → And (LT.lt (Elements.len B C) (Elements.len A D)) (LT.lt (Elements.len F G) (Elements.len B C))
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop15
propositions.enunciation:
Of straight lines in a circle the diameter is greatest, and of the rest the nearer to the centre
is always greater than the more remote.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B D E : Elements.Point} {ABC : Elements.Circle}, Elements.Centre D ABC → Elements.OnCircle A ABC → Elements.Between A D B → Not (Elements.Collinear A B E) → Eq (Elements.ang B A E) Elements.rightAngle → And (∀ (P : Elements.Point), Elements.Collinear A E P → Ne P A → Elements.OutsideCircle P ABC) (∀ (F : Elements.Point), Not (Elements.Collinear A E F) → Exists fun (G : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Collinear A F G) (Elements.InsideCircle G ABC))
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop16
propositions.enunciation:
The straight line drawn at right angles to the diameter of a circle from its extremity will fall
outside the circle, and into the space between the straight line and the circumference another
straight line cannot be interposed; further the angle of the semicircle is greater, and the
remaining angle less, than any acute rectilineal angle.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A : Elements.Point} {BCD : Elements.Circle}, Elements.OutsideCircle A BCD → Exists fun (B : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.OnCircle B BCD) (Elements.Touches A B BCD)
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop17
propositions.enunciation: From a given point to draw a straight line touching a given circle.

propositions.statement: ∀ {C D E F : Elements.Point} {ABC : Elements.Circle}, Elements.Centre F ABC → Elements.OnCircle C ABC → Elements.Touches D E ABC → Elements.Collinear D E C → ∀ (P : Elements.Point), Elements.Collinear D E P → Ne P C → Eq (Elements.ang F C P) Elements.rightAngle
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop18
propositions.enunciation:
If a straight line touch a circle, and a straight line be joined from the centre to the point of
contact, the straight line so joined will be perpendicular to the tangent.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A C D E : Elements.Point} {ABC : Elements.Circle}, Elements.OnCircle C ABC → Elements.Touches D E ABC → Elements.Collinear D E C → Not (Elements.Collinear D E A) → (∀ (P : Elements.Point), Elements.Collinear D E P → Ne P C → Eq (Elements.ang A C P) Elements.rightAngle) → ∀ (F : Elements.Point), Elements.Centre F ABC → Elements.Collinear A C F
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop19
propositions.enunciation:
If a straight line touch a circle, and from the point of contact a straight line be drawn at
right angles to the tangent, the centre of the circle will be on the straight line so drawn.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C K : Elements.Point} {ABC : Elements.Circle}, Elements.OnCircle A ABC → Elements.OnCircle B ABC → Elements.OnCircle C ABC → Elements.OppositeSidesOf A K B C → Eq (Elements.angleAtCentre ABC B K C) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.ang B A C) (Elements.ang B A C))
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop20
propositions.enunciation:
In a circle the angle at the centre is double of the angle at the circumference, when the angles
have the same circumference as base.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B D E : Elements.Point} {ABCD : Elements.Circle}, Elements.OnCircle A ABCD → Elements.OnCircle B ABCD → Elements.OnCircle D ABCD → Elements.OnCircle E ABCD → Elements.SameSideOf A E B D → Eq (Elements.ang B A D) (Elements.ang B E D)
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop21
propositions.enunciation: In a circle the angles in the same segment are equal to one another.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point} {ABCD : Elements.Circle}, Elements.OnCircle A ABCD → Elements.OnCircle B ABCD → Elements.OnCircle C ABCD → Elements.OnCircle D ABCD → Elements.OppositeSidesOf A C B D → And (Eq (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.ang A B C) (Elements.ang A D C)) (HAdd.hAdd Elements.rightAngle Elements.rightAngle)) (Eq (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.ang B A D) (Elements.ang D C B)) (HAdd.hAdd Elements.rightAngle Elements.rightAngle))
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop22
propositions.enunciation: The opposite angles of quadrilaterals in circles are equal to two right angles.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point} {ACB ADB : Elements.Circle}, Elements.OnCircle A ACB → Elements.OnCircle B ACB → Elements.OnCircle C ACB → Elements.OnCircle A ADB → Elements.OnCircle B ADB → Elements.OnCircle D ADB → Elements.SameSideOf C D A B → Eq (Elements.ang A C B) (Elements.ang A D B) → Eq ACB ADB
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop23
propositions.enunciation:
On the same straight line there cannot be constructed two similar and unequal segments of
circles on the same side.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F : Elements.Point} {AEB CFD : Elements.Circle}, Elements.OnCircle A AEB → Elements.OnCircle B AEB → Elements.OnCircle E AEB → Elements.OnCircle C CFD → Elements.OnCircle D CFD → Elements.OnCircle F CFD → Not (Elements.Collinear A B E) → Not (Elements.Collinear C D F) → Eq (Elements.len A B) (Elements.len C D) → Eq (Elements.ang A E B) (Elements.ang C F D) → Elements.Arc.Congruent (Elements.Arc.mk AEB A B E) (Elements.Arc.mk CFD C D F)
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop24
propositions.enunciation: Similar segments of circles on equal straight lines are equal to one another.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A C P : Elements.Point} {S : Elements.Point → Prop}, Not (Elements.Collinear A C P) → (∀ (X Y : Elements.Point), Elements.Between A X C → Elements.SameSideOf Y P A C → Exists fun (B : Elements.Point) => And (S B) (Elements.OnRay B X Y)) → Exists fun (B : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (D : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (E : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (γ : Elements.Circle) => And (S B) (And (Elements.SameSideOf B P A C) (And (Elements.Between A D C) (And (Eq (Elements.len A D) (Elements.len D C)) (And (Eq (Elements.ang A D B) Elements.rightAngle) (And (Elements.Centre E γ) (And (Elements.OnCircle A γ) (And (Elements.OnCircle B γ) (And (Elements.OnCircle C γ) (And (Elements.Collinear D B E) (And (LT.lt (Elements.ang B A D) (Elements.ang A B D) → Elements.OppositeSidesOf E B A C) (And (Eq (Elements.ang A B D) (Elements.ang B A D) → Eq E D) (LT.lt (Elements.ang A B D) (Elements.ang B A D) → Elements.SameSideOf E B A C))))))))))))
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop25
propositions.enunciation: Given a segment of a circle, to describe the complete circle of which it is a segment.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F G H K L : Elements.Point} {ABC DEF : Elements.Circle}, Elements.EqualCircles ABC DEF → Elements.Centre G ABC → Elements.Centre H DEF → Elements.OnCircle A ABC → Elements.OnCircle B ABC → Elements.OnCircle C ABC → Elements.OnCircle D DEF → Elements.OnCircle E DEF → Elements.OnCircle F DEF → Elements.OppositeSidesOf A K B C → Elements.OppositeSidesOf D L E F → And (Elements.OppositeSidesOf G K B C → Elements.OppositeSidesOf H L E F → Eq (Elements.ang B G C) (Elements.ang E H F) → And (Eq (Elements.circumference ABC B K C) (Elements.circumference DEF E L F)) (Elements.Arc.Congruent (Elements.Arc.mk ABC B C K) (Elements.Arc.mk DEF E F L))) (Eq (Elements.ang B A C) (Elements.ang E D F) → And (Eq (Elements.circumference ABC B K C) (Elements.circumference DEF E L F)) (Elements.Arc.Congruent (Elements.Arc.mk ABC B C K) (Elements.Arc.mk DEF E F L)))
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop26
propositions.enunciation:
In equal circles equal angles stand on equal circumferences, whether they stand at the centres
or at the circumferences.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F G H : Elements.Point} {ABC DEF : Elements.Circle}, Elements.EqualCircles ABC DEF → Elements.Centre G ABC → Elements.Centre H DEF → Elements.OnCircle A ABC → Elements.OnCircle B ABC → Elements.OnCircle C ABC → Elements.OnCircle D DEF → Elements.OnCircle E DEF → Elements.OnCircle F DEF → Elements.Triangle B A C → Elements.Triangle E D F → Eq (Elements.standing ABC B A C) (Elements.standing DEF E D F) → And (Eq (Elements.ang B A C) (Elements.ang E D F)) (Elements.SameSideOf G A B C → Elements.SameSideOf H D E F → Eq (Elements.ang B G C) (Elements.ang E H F))
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop27
propositions.enunciation:
In equal circles angles standing on equal circumferences are equal to one another, whether they
stand at the centres or at the circumferences.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F G H : Elements.Point} {ABC DEF : Elements.Circle}, Elements.EqualCircles ABC DEF → Elements.OnCircle A ABC → Elements.OnCircle B ABC → Elements.OnCircle D DEF → Elements.OnCircle E DEF → Elements.OppositeSidesOf C G A B → Elements.OppositeSidesOf F H D E → Eq (Elements.len A B) (Elements.len D E) → LE.le (Elements.circumference ABC A G B) (Elements.circumference ABC A C B) → LE.le (Elements.circumference DEF D H E) (Elements.circumference DEF D F E) → And (And (Eq (Elements.circumference ABC A C B) (Elements.circumference DEF D F E)) (Elements.Arc.Congruent (Elements.Arc.mk ABC A B C) (Elements.Arc.mk DEF D E F))) (And (Eq (Elements.circumference ABC A G B) (Elements.circumference DEF D H E)) (Elements.Arc.Congruent (Elements.Arc.mk ABC A B G) (Elements.Arc.mk DEF D E H)))
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop28
propositions.enunciation:
In equal circles equal straight lines cut off equal circumferences, the greater equal to the
greater and the less to the less.

propositions.statement: ∀ {B C E F G H : Elements.Point} {ABC DEF : Elements.Circle}, Elements.EqualCircles ABC DEF → Elements.OnCircle B ABC → Elements.OnCircle C ABC → Elements.OnCircle E DEF → Elements.OnCircle F DEF → Not (Elements.Collinear B C G) → Not (Elements.Collinear E F H) → Eq (Elements.circumference ABC B G C) (Elements.circumference DEF E H F) → Eq (Elements.len B C) (Elements.len E F)
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop29
propositions.enunciation: In equal circles equal circumferences are subtended by equal straight lines.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B : Elements.Point} {ADB : Elements.Circle}, Elements.OnCircle A ADB → Elements.OnCircle B ADB → ∀ (P : Elements.Point), Not (Elements.Collinear A B P) → Exists fun (D : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.OnCircle D ADB) (And (Elements.SameSideOf D P A B) (Eq (Elements.standing ADB A B D) (Elements.standing ADB D A B)))
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop30
propositions.enunciation: To bisect a given circumference.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C E : Elements.Point} {ABCD : Elements.Circle}, Elements.Centre E ABCD → Elements.OnCircle A ABCD → Elements.OnCircle B ABCD → Elements.OnCircle C ABCD → Elements.Between B E C → Ne A B → Ne A C → And (Eq (Elements.ang B A C) Elements.rightAngle) (And (∀ (X : Elements.Point), Elements.OnCircle X ABCD → Elements.SameSideOf X B A C → LT.lt (Elements.ang A X C) Elements.rightAngle) (∀ (D : Elements.Point), Elements.OnCircle D ABCD → Elements.OppositeSidesOf B D A C → LT.lt Elements.rightAngle (Elements.ang A D C)))
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop31
propositions.enunciation:
In a circle the angle in the semicircle is right, that in a greater segment less than a right
angle, and that in a less segment greater than a right angle; and further the angle of the
greater segment is greater than a right angle, and the angle of the less segment less than a
right angle.

propositions.statement: ∀ {B D E F : Elements.Point} {ABCD : Elements.Circle}, Elements.OnCircle B ABCD → Elements.OnCircle D ABCD → Ne B D → Elements.Touches E F ABCD → Elements.Between E B F → And (∀ (A : Elements.Point), Elements.OnCircle A ABCD → Elements.OppositeSidesOf A F B D → Eq (Elements.ang F B D) (Elements.ang B A D)) (∀ (C : Elements.Point), Elements.OnCircle C ABCD → Elements.SameSideOf C F B D → Eq (Elements.ang E B D) (Elements.ang D C B))
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop32
propositions.enunciation:
If a straight line touch a circle, and from the point of contact there be drawn across, in the
circle, a straight line cutting the circle, the angles which it makes with the tangent will be
equal to the angles in the alternate segments of the circle.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C₁ C C₂ : Elements.Point}, Ne A B → Elements.Triangle C₁ C C₂ → Exists fun (AEB : Elements.Circle) => Exists fun (E : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.OnCircle A AEB) (And (Elements.OnCircle B AEB) (And (Elements.OnCircle E AEB) (And (Not (Elements.Collinear A B E)) (Eq (Elements.ang A E B) (Elements.ang C₁ C C₂)))))
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop33
propositions.enunciation:
On a given straight line to describe a segment of a circle admitting an angle equal to a given
rectilineal angle.

propositions.statement: ∀ {D₁ D D₂ : Elements.Point} (ABC : Elements.Circle), Elements.Triangle D₁ D D₂ → Exists fun (A : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (B : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (C : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.OnCircle A ABC) (And (Elements.OnCircle B ABC) (And (Elements.OnCircle C ABC) (And (Elements.Triangle B A C) (Eq (Elements.ang B A C) (Elements.ang D₁ D D₂)))))
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop34
propositions.enunciation: From a given circle to cut off a segment admitting an angle equal to a given rectilineal angle.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E : Elements.Point} {ABCD : Elements.Circle}, Elements.OnCircle A ABCD → Elements.OnCircle B ABCD → Elements.OnCircle C ABCD → Elements.OnCircle D ABCD → Elements.Between A E C → Elements.Between B E D → Eq (Elements.rect A E E C) (Elements.rect D E E B)
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop35
propositions.enunciation:
If in a circle two straight lines cut one another, the rectangle contained by the segments of
the one is equal to the rectangle contained by the segments of the other.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point} {ABC : Elements.Circle}, Elements.OutsideCircle D ABC → Elements.OnCircle A ABC → Elements.OnCircle B ABC → Elements.OnCircle C ABC → Elements.Between D C A → Elements.Touches D B ABC → Eq (Elements.rect A D D C) (Elements.sq D B)
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop36
propositions.enunciation:
If a point be taken outside a circle and from it there fall on the circle two straight lines,
and if one of them cut the circle and the other touch it, the rectangle contained by the whole
of the straight line which cuts the circle and the straight line intercepted on it outside
between the point and the convex circumference will be equal to the square on the tangent.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D : Elements.Point} {ABC : Elements.Circle}, Elements.OutsideCircle D ABC → Elements.OnCircle A ABC → Elements.OnCircle B ABC → Elements.OnCircle C ABC → Elements.Between D C A → Eq (Elements.rect A D D C) (Elements.sq D B) → Elements.Touches D B ABC
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop37
propositions.enunciation:
If a point be taken outside a circle and from the point there fall on the circle two straight
lines, if one of them cut the circle, and the other fall on it, and if further the rectangle
contained by the whole of the straight line which cuts the circle and the straight line
intercepted on it outside between the point and the convex circumference be equal to the square
on the straight line which falls on the circle, the straight line which falls on it will touch
the circle.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E : Elements.Point}, Elements.Between A E B → Elements.Between C E D → Not (Elements.Collinear A B C) → Eq (HAdd.hAdd (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.ang A E C) (Elements.ang C E B)) (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.ang B E D) (Elements.ang D E A))) (HAdd.hAdd (HAdd.hAdd Elements.rightAngle Elements.rightAngle) (HAdd.hAdd Elements.rightAngle Elements.rightAngle))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop15.porism
propositions.enunciation:
The Porism to I.15: if two straight lines cut one another, the four angles at the point
of section, AEC, CEB, BED and DEA, are together equal to four right angles. It falls
out of I.13, used twice as in I.15 itself, with C.N. 2 to add the two pairs.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D G : Elements.Point} {ABC : Elements.Circle}, Elements.Centre G ABC → Elements.OnCircle A ABC → Elements.OnCircle B ABC → Elements.Between A D B → Eq (Elements.len A D) (Elements.len D B) → Not (Elements.Collinear A B C) → Eq (Elements.ang A D C) Elements.rightAngle → Elements.Collinear D C G
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop1.porism
propositions.enunciation:
The Porism to III.1: "if in a circle a straight line cut a straight line into two
equal parts and at right angles, the centre of the circle is on the cutting straight
line." The straight line DC cuts AB, a straight line in the circle, at its
middle point D and at right angles, and the centre G is on DC. III.9 and III.10
cite it.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A D E : Elements.Point} {ABC : Elements.Circle}, Elements.Centre D ABC → Elements.OnCircle A ABC → Not (Elements.Collinear D A E) → Eq (Elements.ang D A E) Elements.rightAngle → Elements.Touches A E ABC
propositions.name: BookIII.Prop16.porism
propositions.enunciation:
The Porism to III.16: "the straight line drawn at right angles to the diameter of a
circle from its extremity touches the circle." The diameter through A is the
straight line AD, D the centre, and AE is drawn at right angles to it. III.17,
III.33 and III.37 cite it, and Book IV after them.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F : Elements.Point} {L : Elements.Line}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Elements.Triangle D E F → Elements.OnLine B L → Elements.OnLine C L → Elements.OnLine E L → Elements.OnLine F L → Eq (Elements.len B C) (Elements.len E F) → Eq (Elements.area A B C) (Elements.area D E F) → Elements.SameSide A D L → Exists fun (M : Elements.Line) => And (Elements.Parallel M L) (And (Elements.OnLine A M) (Elements.OnLine D M))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop40.general
propositions.enunciation:
**I.40, general** (companion of I.40). Equal triangles ABC, DEF on equal bases BC, EF
of one straight line L, and on the same side of it, are in the same parallels: A and D lie
on one straight line parallel to L. The bases may be apart, touching, overlapping or one,
and named either way along L; the vertices may be one point, and then the parallel is the
one through it.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E F : Elements.Point} {L : Elements.Line}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Elements.Triangle D E F → Elements.OnLine B L → Elements.OnLine C L → Elements.OnLine E L → Elements.OnLine F L → Eq (Elements.len B C) (Elements.len E F) → Eq (Elements.area A B C) (Elements.area D E F) → Elements.SameSide A D L → Ne A D → Elements.AreParallel A D B C
propositions.name: BookI.Prop40.join
propositions.enunciation:
**I.40, the join** (companion of I.40). Under the hypotheses of `Prop40.general`, when
the vertices A and D are two points, the straight line AD joining them is parallel to the
base BC: Euclid's "AD is parallel to BE".

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C D E : Elements.Point}, Elements.Triangle A B C → Elements.Triangle C D E → Elements.Between B C E → Eq (Elements.len B C) (Elements.len C E) → Eq (Elements.area A B C) (Elements.area C D E) → Elements.SameSideOf A D B E → Ne A D → Elements.AreParallel A D B E
propositions.name: BookI.Prop40.special
propositions.enunciation:
**I.40, special** (companion of I.40). The statement of `Prop40`, with the bases BC, CE
end to end, derived from `Prop40.general`: it shows that the general statement contains
Euclid's configuration. The second triangle, CDE, is the triangle DCE on the base
CE, and L is the straight line BE.

propositions.statement: ∀ {E₁ E E₂ : Elements.Point} (R : Elements.Apart), Elements.Triangle E₁ E E₂ → Exists fun (K : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (F : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (L : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (M : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Parallelogram K F L M) (And (Eq (Elements.ang F K M) (Elements.ang E₁ E E₂)) (Eq (Elements.quadArea K F L M) (Elements.Apart.area R)))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop45.apart
propositions.enunciation:
**I.45, for a figure given with triangles that lie apart** (companion of I.45). To
construct, in a given rectilineal angle E, a parallelogram KFLM, its angle at K equal to E,
equal to a given rectilineal figure: the figure given with a checked division into
triangles, any division of it whose triangles lie apart, no point inside two of them
(`Apart`), and "equal to the figure" meaning equal to those triangles taken together
(`Apart.area`). The figure may have a hole, touch itself at a corner, or be in more than one
piece. It is `Prop45.sum` for the figure's triangles;
lying apart is what makes their sum the figure's. The statement speaks of the division given;
that every division of the figure gives the same sum is the content theorem
(`Apart.area_eq_of_same_region`), and the figure by its outline is `Prop45.outline`.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A B C K F L M E₁ E E₂ : Elements.Point}, Elements.Parallelogram K F L M → Eq (Elements.ang F K M) (Elements.ang E₁ E E₂) → Elements.Triangle A B C → Elements.Triangle E₁ E E₂ → Exists fun (K' : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (F' : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (L' : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (M' : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Parallelogram K' F' L' M') (And (Eq (Elements.ang F' K' M') (Elements.ang E₁ E E₂)) (Eq (Elements.quadArea K' F' L' M') (HAdd.hAdd (Elements.quadArea K F L M) (Elements.area A B C))))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop45.append
propositions.enunciation:
**I.45, one more triangle** (companion of I.45). Given a parallelogram KFLM in the
given rectilineal angle E, and a triangle ABC, to construct a parallelogram in the same
angle equal to KFLM and ABC together: the second half of Euclid's proof, which applies a
parallelogram equal to the triangle to a side of the first [I. 44] and shows that the two
make one.

propositions.statement: ∀ {A₀ A₁ A₂ E₁ E E₂ : Elements.Point} {ps : List Elements.Point}, (∀ (s : Prod Elements.Point Elements.Point), Membership.mem (Elements.segments (List.cons A₁ (List.cons A₂ ps))) s → Elements.Triangle A₀ (Prod.fst s) (Prod.snd s)) → (∀ (t : Prod Elements.Point (Prod Elements.Point Elements.Point)), Membership.mem (Elements.triples (List.cons A₁ (List.cons A₂ ps))) t → Elements.OppositeSidesOf (Prod.fst t) (Prod.snd (Prod.snd t)) A₀ (Prod.fst (Prod.snd t))) → LT.lt (Elements.Magnitude.sum (List.map (fun (s : Prod Elements.Point Elements.Point) => Elements.ang (Prod.fst s) A₀ (Prod.snd s)) (Elements.segments (List.cons A₁ (List.cons A₂ ps))))) (HAdd.hAdd (HAdd.hAdd Elements.rightAngle Elements.rightAngle) (HAdd.hAdd Elements.rightAngle Elements.rightAngle)) → Elements.Triangle E₁ E E₂ → Exists fun (R : Elements.Rectilineal) => And (Eq (Elements.Rectilineal.pieces R) (List.map (fun (s : Prod Elements.Point Elements.Point) => Prod.mk A₀ (Prod.mk (Prod.fst s) (Prod.snd s))) (Elements.segments (List.cons A₁ (List.cons A₂ ps))))) (Exists fun (K : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (F : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (L : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (M : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Parallelogram K F L M) (And (Eq (Elements.ang F K M) (Elements.ang E₁ E E₂)) (Eq (Elements.quadArea K F L M) (Elements.Rectilineal.area R))))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop45.fan
propositions.enunciation:
**I.45, for a figure divided from one corner** (companion of I.45), as Euclid and Oliver
Byrne divide it. A figure with corners A₀, A₁, A₂, …, Aₙ, the list `ps` being A₃, …, Aₙ
(empty for a triangle), divided by the straight lines from A₀ into the triangles A₀A₁A₂,
A₀A₂A₃, …, A₀Aₙ₋₁Aₙ, one on each side `segments (A₁ :: A₂ :: ps)`. The division is checked:
each piece is a triangle; each two neighbouring triangles A₀Aᵢ₋₁Aᵢ and A₀AᵢAᵢ₊₁ lie on
opposite sides of the straight line A₀Aᵢ they share (one condition for each of
`triples (A₁ :: A₂ :: ps)`); and the angles A₁A₀A₂, …, Aₙ₋₁A₀Aₙ together are less than four
right angles. Then those triangles, in that order, are fitted together into one figure
(`Fitted.fan`); and, given a rectilineal angle E, there is a parallelogram KFLM, its angle
at K equal to E, equal to that figure, that is, to the triangles taken together. The figure
is the one with corners A₀, A₁, …, Aₙ in order round it, bounded by that closed line
(`Prop45.fan_boundary`), and the triangles' sum is its area, the same for every division of
it (`area_eq`).

The first conclusion is what the two conditions are for: without them the triangles from
A₀ may overlap, and need not be fitted. The parallelogram alone would follow from each
piece being a triangle, by `Prop45.sum`.

Euclid's ABCD with DB joined is the figure with corners D, A, B, C, its triangles DAB and
DBC: A and C lie on opposite sides of DB. Byrne's figure has its corners listed from its
re-entrant corner, from which both his straight lines are drawn.

propositions.statement: ∀ {E₁ E E₂ : Elements.Point} (R : Elements.Rectilineal), Elements.Triangle E₁ E E₂ → Exists fun (K : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (F : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (L : Elements.Point) => Exists fun (M : Elements.Point) => And (Elements.Parallelogram K F L M) (And (Eq (Elements.ang F K M) (Elements.ang E₁ E E₂)) (Eq (Elements.quadArea K F L M) (Elements.Rectilineal.area R)))
propositions.name: BookI.Prop45.figure
propositions.enunciation:
**I.45, for a figure with one boundary, given with triangles fitted together**
(companion of I.45). To construct, in a given rectilineal angle E, a parallelogram KFLM,
its angle at K equal to E, equal to a given rectilineal figure: the figure given with a
checked division into triangles, fitted together in a suitable order, each glued across a
side of an earlier one and meeting the earlier ones only along it (`Rectilineal`), and
"equal to the figure" meaning equal to those triangles taken together (`Rectilineal.area`). The figure may be convex or not, and need have no corner from
which the straight lines to the others divide it. It is `Prop45.apart` for the figure's
triangles, which lie apart (`Fitted.inside_pairwise`, `Rectilineal.toApart`). As there, the
